reviews.title: Très décevant
reviews.text: Alors que je mettrai 5* à la version PC, là je mettrai 0,5* si c’était possible. L’application est lourde l’édition maladroite. Oui on peut lire des partitions mais même ça c’est un peu limité, l’application est agaçante, l’ergonomie peu pratique. Alors oui on peut éditer une ligne de musique mais c’est pas intuitif on peut pas utiliser le stylet de l’iPad, j’aurais accepté de payer le même prix que l’application PC. Là, c’est une application « bateau », histoire d’exister. Dommage, il y a des concurrents qui commencent à arriver et à mon avis, prendre la place bien que ce soit sous forme d’abonnement.

reviews.title: Useless to compose with
reviews.text: I  own Guitar Pro 8 on computer and have composed 10-minute-long multi-track songs with it (well, usually GP v5.2 which is overall better), and the best they can do on the mobile version is give "Notepad" for jotting down absolute bare-minimum ideas, with no integration to the PC software? And using a keyboard on iPad (3rd party keyboard in my case) provides NO input i.e. arrow keys, pressing numbers for note entry, even in Notepad. The absolute most French thing you could do to maintain a software product ecosystem for people who compose via tablature. What a joke. I hope Dorico continues improving their guitar tablature features on both PC and mobile so I can finally ahve tablature-first composition in a software ecosystem that takes itself, its customer-base, and the entire idea seriously and approaches things with a bit of enthusiasm instead of the entitled Malaise the people at Arobas Music have, despite the many stereotypes about the French, they're ticking every box and have been  for decades. *spits*

reviews.title: Inquiétude sur l’avenir
reviews.text:
J’utilise Guitar Pro sur Mac depuis plusieurs années avec ses mises à jour successives et j’en suis pleinement satisfait. J’ai aussi acquis la version pour iPad qui comme plusieurs utilisateurs l’ont noté n’est pas du tout du même niveau. Plusieurs vidéos ont annoncé une nouvelle version plus respectueuse des partitions pour iOS mais celle-ci n’est malheureusement toujours pas disponible.
Récemment, j’ai souhaité acquérir une partition sur MySongBook. Un problème est survenu et je n’ai pu récupérer ma licence. En soi c’est possible mais j’ai laissé plusieurs messages au support restés sans réponse. le service commercial est sur répondeur et malgré un nouveau message laissé je n’ai aucune nouvelle.
Mon sentiment est que ce qui était un excellent logiciel, de plus français, est aujourd’hui laissé à l’abandon.

reviews.title: Trash vs Desktop
reviews.text: For anyone without access to a computer at all times who likes to jot down an abundance of ideas, GP iOS consistently falls short. I have had so many great ideas erased just by switching instruments it causes unbelievable frustration. Instead of designing some kind of failsafe feature to preserve notes after switching instruments, this app will automatically erase 2 lowest string notes after switching guitar sounds when using 8 string instruments. I would love to be able to do some simple layering of instruments so I can have a bass and guitar play together, but this isn’t possible in the notepad feature. I find myself trying to use one single staff to harmonize and then separate them later on the computer version. Not sure why this app was designed to be so disappointing in so many ways… Please improve features above and maybe I could provide a better review.

reviews.title: Lackluster Compared to Desktop Application
reviews.text:
I use guitar pro 8 on my computer almost every day when practicing. I've used the mobile app maybe 5 times. I wouldn't recommend the mobile app unless you absolutely need to write tabs in a life or death situation. Even if you don't own a computer, I'd recommend other options first.

The midi audio quality is alright. It's almost like 8 bit sounds, which is kinda cool, but terrible compared to the desktop application. I'm not expecting modern sounding midi guitar from the mobile app, so it's not really my biggest complaint though. It's more that the articulations such as palm muting, slides, and bends can be bad.

Writing tabs on the app is abysmal. I've done it once to remember something, but it was almost not worth it.

You cannot add an audio file to the tabs like you can on desktop. So if you have jam tracks that you'd like to sync up to the tabs, you won't be doing that on mobile. Adding this feature would sort of negate my complaint about the audio. If I could sync an audio file to the tabs, I would just mute the tabs and only play the audio.

reviews.title: Useless
reviews.text: It used to be that the guitar pro community was about people making and sharing tabs, but now guitar pro has gone full Roblox everything is a subscription. You can’t edit music with this app, so it’s only a reader. However, you can only now get guitar tabs (overwhelmingly made for free by other users) by going through one or more paywalls. Considering that most of the tabs are incorrect (which was fine when they were free), that’s ridiculous. Given the extremely minor functionality of this app, it should be free, too.

reviews.title: iPad Disappointment
reviews.text: New to GP, I got quite excited about using Guitar Pro on my Mac Studio while learning to add a bass track to a .gp file a bandmate shared with me. I was so excited I added GP to my iPad. Unfortunately, my iPad experience was completely opposite. The mobile version of GP falls so far short of the Mac app… It’s pretty much useless. I am going to continue using GP on my Mac. It’s a great tool. But, it certainly lacks in portability. Here’s hoping this gets fixed soon. Maybe GP9?
